angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 46,138,128 km at 102.14 pc = 6.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56211: distance 102.145 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.015), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 102.145 +/- 1.532 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.6458 +/- 0.1446 mas (same row, RUWE 2.48), 59.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 66.319 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56211: radius 66.319 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 811.02 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.068) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 46,138,128 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 3785 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56211: effective temperature 3785 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.053) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56211: effective temperature 3785 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.053) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
